sourceLongSummaries: The party flies west past statues of the Warlord and Wildling. After a couple of hours, an oppressive presence pushes at them as they approach the tower. Seeker lands behind a boulder, animates the rope ladder, and transforms it into another osprey. They inspect the tower’s terrace, two stone guardians with metal fists, and a hatch at the top of the spire.

Crystal darts strike the birds just before they land, breaking several transformations and leaving Seeker hurt from the fall. The party gathers on the roof and investigates the handleless hatch with mundane inspection, Detect Magic, and Tremorsense. They prepare to use the chime under Silence, but the guardians move before that precaution can be completed.

A tiny mechanical fly has been observing the party as the guardians rise toward the roof. Wellby opens the hatch with the chime and jumps through, while Kenzo carries Seeker inside. Delwath follows after taking a dart hit and closes the hatch. Below it, they find an anvil, hanging manacles, channels leading to a well, and descending stairs.

Putting blood on the anvil has no apparent effect. Seeker touches the necromantic manacles to identify them, resists their influence, and learns that they channel sacrificed souls into a nearby phylactery and help prepare a potion for lich transformation. The party considers using the mirror to discover Apollyon’s phylactery, but hears the guardians approaching from below.

Kenzo takes a flying position above the stairs, the animated ladder blocks the passage, and Wellby prepares to shoot from behind it. Delwath conjures shadowy lynxes, but their attacks gain no purchase on the guardians. Seeker retains concentration on Animal Shapes while the party works around the cramped approach and the constructs’ magical defenses.

Wellby shoots the first guardian’s eyes, giving Kenzo an opening for a flurry of attacks. The guardians batter the ladder and fire force darts, but cannot shove the oversized barricade aside. Delwath struggles to reach the enemy through the crowded stairway.

Delwath casts Sanctuary on the ladder, then discovers that an acid Sorcerer Burst rebounds from the guardian toward Kenzo, who deflects it harmlessly. Seeker becomes a large bird and inspires Kenzo while the ladder holds its position. Wellby blinds the guardian again so Kenzo can continue attacking.

Kenzo deflects one punch but is knocked backward by another and wounded by darts. Delwath drops into the space between the guardians and strikes with a smite, leaving the leading construct badly damaged. Seeker attacks in bird form while the ladder continues to contest the passage.

Wellby shifts his blinding arrows to the second guardian as Kenzo destroys the first and flies around the survivor. Kenzo turns its punches back against it, Seeker attacks in bird form, and Delwath protects himself with Shield. Delwath’s final sword strike brings down the remaining guardian.

The party heals Kenzo and the ladder, then retrieves two cracked metallic cores and two mechanical flies from the guardians’ remains. They weigh the mirror’s seven-day recharge against other questions they may need to ask. Since the manacles are fixed in place, they choose to investigate them now and hope to retain another use for Rai’s hand later.

Kenzo asks the mirror to show the phylactery. The vision depicts a human Apollyon wearing a crown and rainbow cloak, forging an unadorned iron-hilted dagger with layers of inscribed adamantine. Repeated sacrifices send souls into the dagger, while collected blood and shadows from the crown contribute to his potion. Seeker searches for adamantine and gathers about half a pound of scraps, hoping they might help locate the dagger.

An empty terrace, decayed study, and largely ruined library yield two intact books: an unmarked crimson volume and a locked book with a metal clasp. Seeker discovers that the crimson book is bound in human skin soaked in blood and explains how to become a lich. After handling it, he undergoes an unexplained saving throw; the party uses Mage Hand to place both books in the portable hole.

They pass an Omnis Pura meeting room with imperial statues, then hear metal rattling beyond a partition. Delwath’s Ghostly Gaze reveals scraps swirling in the next room. Rather than enter it, the party flies outside as ospreys and reenters through lower windows. Searching three residential floors yields coins, a silver pitcher, a gold platter, and three plain gold rings.

At the entrance level, Seeker detects extensive rooms below and the party finds a stairway in a side guardroom. Wellby checks the audience chamber before they descend. Roughly forty skeletons, including one on the throne, begin to rise, so the party shuts the doors and braces them with an immovable rod.

Seeker and Delwath fly outside as birds to attack through the windows. Once they resume their normal forms, the book’s curse makes Seeker strike Delwath with Catapult; a black shadow leaves Seeker’s face, and he remembers none of it. Delwath’s Sickening Radiance kills the skeletons over ten minutes. Seeker heals Delwath and Kenzo’s cleansing touch confirms that the influence has departed.

With the skeletons destroyed, the party claims the large gemstone-studded stone throne. They rearrange the portable hole, moving its mirrors out of the way, and use Animal Shapes to become elephants capable of pushing the throne inside. They then repack the hole around their new prize.

The basement contains spoiled wine and moldy silk, with another stairway descending to a locked metal door. Wellby finds no physical trap, while Detect Magic detects magic beyond the barrier. After roughly an hour of searching since the guardian fight, they return upstairs for a short rest with Delwath’s tea and biscuits; the ladder’s animation expires.

Delwath’s Ghostly Gaze reveals a pedestal with four openings and ten silver rings connected to a wall plate, a floating sword like a hole in the world, and two side rooms. See Invisibility exposes two large force hands. The party spreads out before Wellby unlocks the door and triggers a fireball; Wellby evades the blast, but Seeker takes 32 points of fire damage despite spending heroic inspiration.

As initiative begins, Seeker reanimates the ladder instead of using a concentration-dependent summoned construct. Kenzo’s Soul Sight reveals the void sword’s formidable defenses, including immunity to psychic, necrotic, and poison damage and all conditions. The party plans to fill the forge with Sickening Radiance, shut the door, and withdraw.

Delwath fills the forge with Sickening Radiance and Kenzo shuts the door as they retreat. The sword slips through the barrier and stabs Wellby and the ladder. Radiance reveals one invisible hand. Seeker converts Psychic Disruption into fire with his glove to wound the sword, then withdraws as Wellby strains to keep the hands behind the door.

A hand bursts through the doorway and knocks Wellby prone. He scrambles away, stands, and lands a critical arrow that badly damages the sword. The ladder keeps striking it, but the sword acts again, stabbing the ladder and Seeker while Kenzo prepares to use his tattoo’s reach.

Kenzo reaches the sword with Lengau’s Claw, avoiding psychic attacks that cannot harm it. After considering a wider teleport, Delwath uses Scatter to move himself and Seeker, taking Seeker out of immediate danger and entering melee. He withstands the sword’s retaliation and lands a critical Eldritch Smite.

Delwath’s blow shatters the sword into four independently attacking daggers. He uses Shield against their initial assault, though one wounds him. Seeker drops Animal Shapes and casts Slow on three daggers, ending the party’s easy flight home. The ladder grapples a force hand while Wellby destroys the unslowed dagger with a critical shot.

Kenzo and Delwath destroy two of the remaining daggers; the last evades Seeker’s Catapult before Kenzo finishes it. Wellby brings down the rear force hand with his fiery bow. The front hand shoves the ladder backward and knocks it prone, but Wellby destroys that hand as well, leaving the party free to enter the forge.

Using the last moments of Ghostly Gaze and Seeker’s Tremorsense, the party checks for more threats. One room holds roughly two hundred bars of silver, mithril, and unfamiliar metals, but no adamantine. Wellby unlocks a stone chest containing a damaged silver rod with organic spiral decoration and a star-like orb, twenty labeled boxes of magical powders, and rings.

The chest’s three matching braided-gold rings bear emerald, ruby, and sapphire, while the other side room holds mundane etching chemicals. Kenzo senses no ley lines at the forge. In response to Delwath’s five questions, the Tanshi indicate that touching it is not known to be dangerous, it remains functional, the user powers it, instructions survive in the notes, and its price is complicated. The party leaves the mechanism untouched.

They take the rod, powders, and rings upstairs. The portable hole smells of blood from the crimson book, so they remove both books. Wellby spots a tiny protective glyph on the locked book’s clasp. Two attempts to dispel it fail, and they decide to use the chime from as far away as possible with the others around a corner.

recapBlocks.title: Scouting and Departure
sourceShortSummaries: The party surveys Circular Island from the mountaintop and considers investigating Apollyon’s tower.
In a flashback to the previous evening, Seeker scouts the dragon’s lair with Clairvoyance.
The party takes leave of Dimitaur and chooses the tower as its first destination.
Seeker prepares to transform the party into ordinary ospreys for the westward flight.
sourceLongSummaries: After resting at the temple, the party watches sunrise over the island’s radiating rivers and pools. Apollyon’s black tower remains conspicuously intact to the west. They discuss visiting it and investigating the dragon’s territory, then return to reconnaissance that could have happened before the preceding night’s rest.

Before the previous long rest, Seeker uses three Clairvoyance charges to inspect a ruined villa, a plaza, and thermal pools amid red-orange growth. Dragonets and four chimeras are visible. Kenzo cannot sense the dragon’s aura, prompting speculation about an extradimensional lair, but detects a fiend beneath the villa.

Back in the morning, Kenzo gives Dimitaur a statue of himself before the party leaves. They prioritize the tower and its possible forge over the dragon and jade. Kenzo senses no conscious creatures at the tower, although this cannot exclude constructs, mindless undead, or traps, and the party weighs travel options for the jagged coast.

The party chooses inconspicuous ordinary ospreys rather than larger birds. Seeker’s Animal Shapes will carry them to the tower, with an expected flight of several hours. They plan to animate the rope ladder close to the destination so its shorter duration will not expire during the journey.

sourceShortSummaries: Seeker identifies the manacles as instruments for capturing sacrificed souls and creating a lich.
The party holds the narrow stairs while the guardians advance into the ritual chamber.
Wellby blinds the leading guardian while the ladder absorbs its counterattack.
A reflected spell forces the party to rely on arrows, strikes, and the ladder’s defense.
Kenzo is driven back as Delwath and Seeker press the attack at the stairway.
Kenzo and Delwath finish the two guardians, leaving only dust and mechanical remains.
sourceLongSummaries: Putting blood on the anvil has no apparent effect. Seeker touches the necromantic manacles to identify them, resists their influence, and learns that they channel sacrificed souls into a nearby phylactery and help prepare a potion for lich transformation. The party considers using the mirror to discover Apollyon’s phylactery, but hears the guardians approaching from below.

Kenzo takes a flying position above the stairs, the animated ladder blocks the passage, and Wellby prepares to shoot from behind it. Delwath conjures shadowy lynxes, but their attacks gain no purchase on the guardians. Seeker retains concentration on Animal Shapes while the party works around the cramped approach and the constructs’ magical defenses.

Wellby shoots the first guardian’s eyes, giving Kenzo an opening for a flurry of attacks. The guardians batter the ladder and fire force darts, but cannot shove the oversized barricade aside. Delwath struggles to reach the enemy through the crowded stairway.

Delwath casts Sanctuary on the ladder, then discovers that an acid Sorcerer Burst rebounds from the guardian toward Kenzo, who deflects it harmlessly. Seeker becomes a large bird and inspires Kenzo while the ladder holds its position. Wellby blinds the guardian again so Kenzo can continue attacking.

Kenzo deflects one punch but is knocked backward by another and wounded by darts. Delwath drops into the space between the guardians and strikes with a smite, leaving the leading construct badly damaged. Seeker attacks in bird form while the ladder continues to contest the passage.

Wellby shifts his blinding arrows to the second guardian as Kenzo destroys the first and flies around the survivor. Kenzo turns its punches back against it, Seeker attacks in bird form, and Delwath protects himself with Shield. Delwath’s final sword strike brings down the remaining guardian.

sourceShortSummaries: Wellby opens the audience chamber, awakens its skeletons, and seals the doors with an immovable rod.
The party destroys the trapped skeletons while a possessing shadow briefly forces Seeker to attack Delwath.
The party becomes elephants to push the jeweled throne into the portable hole.
A locked door below the storage rooms prompts a short rest before further exploration.
After scouting the hidden forge, the party opens its door and triggers a fireball trap.
sourceLongSummaries: At the entrance level, Seeker detects extensive rooms below and the party finds a stairway in a side guardroom. Wellby checks the audience chamber before they descend. Roughly forty skeletons, including one on the throne, begin to rise, so the party shuts the doors and braces them with an immovable rod.

Seeker and Delwath fly outside as birds to attack through the windows. Once they resume their normal forms, the book’s curse makes Seeker strike Delwath with Catapult; a black shadow leaves Seeker’s face, and he remembers none of it. Delwath’s Sickening Radiance kills the skeletons over ten minutes. Seeker heals Delwath and Kenzo’s cleansing touch confirms that the influence has departed.

With the skeletons destroyed, the party claims the large gemstone-studded stone throne. They rearrange the portable hole, moving its mirrors out of the way, and use Animal Shapes to become elephants capable of pushing the throne inside. They then repack the hole around their new prize.

The basement contains spoiled wine and moldy silk, with another stairway descending to a locked metal door. Wellby finds no physical trap, while Detect Magic detects magic beyond the barrier. After roughly an hour of searching since the guardian fight, they return upstairs for a short rest with Delwath’s tea and biscuits; the ladder’s animation expires.

Delwath’s Ghostly Gaze reveals a pedestal with four openings and ten silver rings connected to a wall plate, a floating sword like a hole in the world, and two side rooms. See Invisibility exposes two large force hands. The party spreads out before Wellby unlocks the door and triggers a fireball; Wellby evades the blast, but Seeker takes 32 points of fire damage despite spending heroic inspiration.

recapBlocks.title: The Forge’s Defenders
sourceShortSummaries: The party rolls initiative against the void sword and force hands and plans to contain them with Sickening Radiance.
The void sword passes through the closed door while the force hands push after it.
The hands force the door open as Wellby critically wounds the sword and retreats.
Delwath uses Scatter to rescue Seeker and places himself beside the sword for a critical smite.
The sword breaks into four void daggers, and Seeker sacrifices Animal Shapes to slow three of them.
The party destroys the remaining daggers and both force hands while the ladder holds the passage.
sourceLongSummaries: As initiative begins, Seeker reanimates the ladder instead of using a concentration-dependent summoned construct. Kenzo’s Soul Sight reveals the void sword’s formidable defenses, including immunity to psychic, necrotic, and poison damage and all conditions. The party plans to fill the forge with Sickening Radiance, shut the door, and withdraw.

Delwath fills the forge with Sickening Radiance and Kenzo shuts the door as they retreat. The sword slips through the barrier and stabs Wellby and the ladder. Radiance reveals one invisible hand. Seeker converts Psychic Disruption into fire with his glove to wound the sword, then withdraws as Wellby strains to keep the hands behind the door.

A hand bursts through the doorway and knocks Wellby prone. He scrambles away, stands, and lands a critical arrow that badly damages the sword. The ladder keeps striking it, but the sword acts again, stabbing the ladder and Seeker while Kenzo prepares to use his tattoo’s reach.

Kenzo reaches the sword with Lengau’s Claw, avoiding psychic attacks that cannot harm it. After considering a wider teleport, Delwath uses Scatter to move himself and Seeker, taking Seeker out of immediate danger and entering melee. He withstands the sword’s retaliation and lands a critical Eldritch Smite.

Delwath’s blow shatters the sword into four independently attacking daggers. He uses Shield against their initial assault, though one wounds him. Seeker drops Animal Shapes and casts Slow on three daggers, ending the party’s easy flight home. The ladder grapples a force hand while Wellby destroys the unslowed dagger with a critical shot.

Kenzo and Delwath destroy two of the remaining daggers; the last evades Seeker’s Catapult before Kenzo finishes it. Wellby brings down the rear force hand with his fiery bow. The front hand shoves the ladder backward and knocks it prone, but Wellby destroys that hand as well, leaving the party free to enter the forge.

recapBlocks.title: Secrets and the Return to Dimitaur
sourceShortSummaries: The forge’s side rooms contain metal stock and a locked chest of magical supplies.
The Tanshi confirm that the forge still works and draws its power from the user.
The party finds a glyph protecting Apollyon’s locked spellbook and prepares to open it from a distance.
After the book’s glyph wounds Wellby, Seeker deciphers Apollyon’s instructions for powering the forge.
At sunset the party returns to Dimitaur, who destroys the dangerous crimson book with fire.
sourceLongSummaries: Using the last moments of Ghostly Gaze and Seeker’s Tremorsense, the party checks for more threats. One room holds roughly two hundred bars of silver, mithril, and unfamiliar metals, but no adamantine. Wellby unlocks a stone chest containing a damaged silver rod with organic spiral decoration and a star-like orb, twenty labeled boxes of magical powders, and rings.

The chest’s three matching braided-gold rings bear emerald, ruby, and sapphire, while the other side room holds mundane etching chemicals. Kenzo senses no ley lines at the forge. In response to Delwath’s five questions, the Tanshi indicate that touching it is not known to be dangerous, it remains functional, the user powers it, instructions survive in the notes, and its price is complicated. The party leaves the mechanism untouched.

They take the rod, powders, and rings upstairs. The portable hole smells of blood from the crimson book, so they remove both books. Wellby spots a tiny protective glyph on the locked book’s clasp. Two attempts to dispel it fail, and they decide to use the chime from as far away as possible with the others around a corner.

The chime opens the book but triggers its glyph; Wellby suffers a powerful psychic blast while resisting its lasting mental effect. The volume contains backup spells and encrypted research notes, including forge instructions written in Elvish. Seeker spends three hours deciphering them, from about midafternoon to six, while companions rest. The forge consumes the user’s highest spell slot, recovered only after successful daily checks, and combines etched metal, powders, a hand plate, and an item opening. The rod appears to have been damaged in an attempt to destroy it, and the rings seem to have been found rather than made; their origins remain uncertain.

Seeker encloses the lich book in a temporarily created lead box, and the party teleports back to the Sibyl’s temple at sunset. They ask Dimitaur to watch the dangerous book while they investigate the dragon the following day. Instead, he orders them clear, opens the box, and burns the book with a fireball. They report their tower discoveries and prepare to rest; no following morning occurs before the session ends.
